notes.title: Sticker Delight Update #3: Introducing Sticker Book in The Game
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello Everyone,[/h3]

We have two exciting updates to share this time! ✨

[h3]Introducing: Sticker Book Feature[/h3]
We have finally finished developing a delightful new feature for the game:[b] the Sticker Book[/b]. You will be able to access the Sticker Book after completing dinner for the first time. Inside the Sticker Book, you can:
[list]
[*] Reminisce about the memories by keeping photos taken during dinner
[*] Choose and keep your favorite stickers from the pack
[*] Express yourself using stickers from the pack and text stickers that you create (we've also included a screenshot and download button, so you can share it with your loved ones)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45077900/4aeb991592017a8cd4766767b4408c62167bb12c.gif[/img]

While this might not be obvious, we also believe that the Sticker Book is a versatile tool that you can keep coming back to in the future to express your thoughts to loved ones!
It works like this: Open the Sticker Book → express your thoughts → screenshot and download → share it to your loved ones → repeat

[h3]Sticker Delight is Nominated as SEA Game Awards 2024 Finalist![/h3] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45077900/9a09554312d218d5a15ea9b9441ec2bde738efe6.png[/img]
Earlier this month, we received an announcement that Sticker Delight has been nominated for the SEA Game Awards 2024 ([url=https://fb.watch/up9qflwQKM/]public announcement here[/url])! The final results will be announced on October 2, and we're sharing this joy to spread positive energy to everyone following our news 😊

I'll catch you in the next post,
[b]Li
Producer - Sticker Delight[/b]

notes.title: Sticker Delight Update #2: How Sticker Delight Started (a Devlog)
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello Everyone,[/h3]

Welcome back! This time, I've brought along my fellow team members and we'll be sharing some stories behind Sticker Delight.

[h2]How did Sticker Delight start?[/h2]
Earlier this year, I (Li) pitched a wholesome game idea about bringing players to reminisce childhood, revolving around stickers and food.
 
Once pre-production wrapped up, the game idea really took shape: play as a child who completes errands to prepare a New Year's dinner for family and friends.

Fast forward to now, we're on our way to finishing Sticker Delight soon. Time really flies.

[h2]Who's developing Sticker Delight?[/h2]
We're making Sticker Delight with following team:
- I (Li) am in charge of producing and design,
- Riady is in charge of programming, 
- Cc is in charge of art

[h2]What did we explore in the beginning?[/h2]
[b]Design[/b]
Li: As far as I remember, the first thing I explored was sticker puzzles. I asked myself, "How Might We use stickers to progress in the game?"

I played around with stickers and ended up designing multiple sticker puzzles. 
Here's the evolution of one of our sticker puzzles:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45077900/f7739758edce1622061897690948cf5216684dae.png[/img]

[b]Art[/b]
Cc: My first step was to create the visual foundation for the game. I started by creating a mood board to capture the cozy and inviting atmosphere we wanted to convey. I led the team to brainstorm together for making the mood board. 

Using that mood board as inspiration, I experimented with different art styles to find the perfect match for our game. It was a fun process exploring various looks until we finally found a style that could represent everything we wanted to convey in this game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45077900/c9d389c89e239e31377818329154acd414a2ed5f.gif[/img]

[b]Tech[/b]
Riady: Since the core mechanic we wanted in this game was dragging and dropping objects under certain rule, such as "the sticker must cover X area" or "the sticker must be within X area," the first thing I did was create a simple gameplay prototype to cover those aspects. Initially, I struggled with the "sticker must cover X area" mechanic. I thought I needed a complex math formula to calculate the surface area considered "covered" by other objects. However, after some thought, I found a better solution by using many small colliders within the image. When the player drops the object, it checks each individual small collider. If all the colliders are checked, then the object is considered "covered."

***
That's it for today's update! 
Catch you in the next post,

[b]Li
Producer - Sticker Delight[/b]

notes.title: Sticker Delight Update #1: Gameplay Video & Participation in The HARGAI 2024
notes.notes:
[h3]Hello Everyone,[/h3]

We have two exciting updates to share this time! ✨

[h3]We have uploaded the gameplay video for Sticker Delight[/h3]
The gameplay video is available on our Store page here: 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3053210?utm_source=steamnews
Feel free to let us know what you think about the gameplay video in the discussion 😊

[h3]Sticker Delight is included in the HARGAI 2024 Steam Sale Event[/h3] 
Organized by the Indonesian Game Association (AGI) to celebrate Indonesia's Game Day on August 8, we submitted Sticker Delight to be included in the HARGAI 2024 Steam Sale Event (running until August 31) alongside other released and upcoming games. It's our first time participating in a Steam Sale Event, and we hope to reach more cozy gamers and sticker lovers through this event. 

During the sale event, multiple titles offer exciting discounts. The Steam Sale Event can be accessed here: https://store.steampowered.com/sale/hargai2024?tab=5.


Thank you for loving Sticker Delight, and I'll catch you in the next post,
[b]Li
Producer - Sticker Delight[/b]
